tools.name: fcart_reset_license
tools.description: Return an active license to the never-activated state: detach every activation, recount, then set the status to "inactive" (REST update_status cannot set inactive). Only an active or inactive license is reset; a disabled or expired one is refused, since inactive counts as usable and the reset would undo the revocation (set it active with fcart_update_license_status first if re-enabling is intended). Defaults to a dry run that changes nothing and returns the current status, the activations (masked) and the planned steps, naming any other license that shares a site about to be deleted. A real run needs dry_run:false AND confirm:true (booleans). It detaches each activation through FluentCart's own admin deactivate_site, stopping at the first error and reporting what was already detached, and only then recounts and sets inactive, because FluentCart's recount flips inactive back to active. WARNING: each detach also deletes that activation's shared site row (see fcart_deactivate_license_site). A license reset to inactive cannot be activated through admin activate_site until it is set active again (FluentCart treats inactive as invalid there); SyteOps 1.6.732's gateway makes that switch. Requires the FluentCart licenses/manage permission.

confirm.description: Required (true), together with dry_run:false, for a real run.

Under a credential-shaped name a number is still returned when its key ends in a structural measure (session_timeout, nonce_lifetime, cache_ttl, token_ttl, token_expiry, key_length, password_min_length, max_login_attempts, api_version), and a string under cache_key, meta_key, sort_key, transient_key, foreign_key, column_key or index_key when it is a plain identifier. A string that looks like a credential is hidden whatever it is called (fail closed: an unbroken 16+ character string unless it is an email, clean URL, hostname, date, number, version or lowercase slug). Credential rows are allowlist-only: flowmattic_settings exposes notification_email and notification_email_connect; sq_options and fluentmail-settings are refused (use the sqseo_* and fsmtp_* tools). SyteWide MCP API keys, SyteOps keys and licensing, WordPress salts and the role map report only {exists}.

tools.name: replace_content_text
tools.description: Replace exact text in one or more posts or Elementor pages, all or nothing. Defaults to a dry run that writes nothing and previews every edit (match counts, where found as widget and setting, the post_content mirror count, what would be written). A real run needs dry_run:false AND confirm:true. Every edit is checked before any write: each must match old exactly expected_count times (default 1), so one bad edit writes nothing and the result names it. On an Elementor page only the matching setting values change and the rest of _elementor_data stays byte for byte; post_content (the mirror) must hold old the same number of times and gets the same replacement. widget_id limits an Elementor match to one widget; refuse_if_present refuses a post that already contains a string (use the target URL to prevent double links). A match inside an HTML tag (an attribute) is refused unless allow_in_attributes:true; a match inside <script>, <style> or an HTML comment is refused unless allow_in_code:true. A restore point (a revision carrying the Elementor meta) is created per post before writing and must still exist; the result gives revision_id, the sha1 of the old _elementor_data and rollback steps. Writes are raw compare-and-swap SQL (no kses, no second revision): a post changed by someone else in the meantime is refused untouched and the posts already written are put back. Save hooks do not run; post_modified is set, caches are cleared and SyteOps cache.purge runs when available. A builder-mode Elementor page with no usable _elementor_data is refused. With verify_rendered (default true) it fetches each published post of this site (about 20 s in total, then the rest are skipped with time_budget) and warns when the new text is missing from the rendered page (it may be stripped from display, for example an in-body FAQ replaced by structured data): check those warnings, the write has already happened. Takes 1-25 edits, one per post. Same permission as update_content (edit_post per post); without unfiltered_html, the stored result must pass wp_kses_post() unchanged and carry no disallowed URL protocol, only Elementor text and content settings may change (not links, custom attributes, CSS, ids or dynamic tags), and allow_in_attributes / allow_in_code are refused.

expected_count.description: How many times old must occur (default 1). Any other count refuses the edit.

widget_id.description: Elementor only: match only in this widget's settings.

refuse_if_present.description: Refuse the edit if the post already contains this string, for example the target URL.

allow_in_attributes.description: Default false: refuse a match that falls inside an HTML tag, so only text content changes.

allow_in_code.description: Default false: refuse a match inside <script>, <style> or an HTML comment (JSON-LD, CSS, notes). Separate from allow_in_attributes.

dry_run.description: Default true: preview only. Pass false (with confirm:true) to write.

confirm.description: Required (true), together with dry_run:false, for a real write.

verify_rendered.description: Default true: after writing, fetch each published post and warn when the new text is not in the rendered HTML.

dry_run.description: If true, preview this destructive action without executing it.

tools.name: syteops_builder_guard
tools.description: Read-only. Recompute the agent-prompt guard hash (CANON-1) for one Elementor element (SyteOps builder.guard). Call it right before an Elementor MCP write and compare it with the task's guard; if they differ the element changed, so stop. Never hash by hand. Returns {status, reason, guard, guard_keys, widget_type}, never a setting value. Check status first: when the element can't be resolved (bad el_id, not found, ambiguous) the call still succeeds, with a reason and an empty guard, so two empty guards matching proves nothing. post_id may be a page or a published Elementor template (elementor_library); syteops_seo_get and syteops_seo_set refuse templates. An API key is trusted; a signed-in caller needs edit access to the post. Errors: post_not_found (trashed or not viewable), forbidden (no edit access), module_unavailable (Review Portal not loaded). Note for the write that follows: EMCP update-element and update-widget merge settings shallowly, so writing __globals__ or link replaces that whole object; send every key it should keep.

tools.name: syteops_cache_purge
tools.description: Purge one post's page, or up to 30 URLs on this site, from LiteSpeed and Cloudflare when present (SyteOps cache.purge). Send post_id or urls, not both. Prefer post_id: only that path also clears Elementor's generated CSS (site-wide, and only when the post is built with Elementor; elementor_css reports cleared, unavailable or not_elementor). A URL on another host refuses the whole call. Returns {urls, purged, attempted, skipped, errors, elementor_css}.

urls.description: Absolute http(s) URLs on this site's host, at most 30.

tools.name: syteops_calendar_check
tools.description: Read-only advisory: would scheduling this post at this moment break the site's publishing rhythm, and where would it fit instead? (SyteOps calendar.cadence_check; SyteOps 1.6.758+). Nothing is written or refused. scope is all (default) or pipeline. Returns {post_id, date_gmt, enabled, collides, reasons[], conflicts[], suggestion_label, suggestion_local, truncated}. Returns 409 module_unavailable when Content Pipelines is not active.

date.description: ISO 8601 date-time, e.g. 2026-11-03T09:00:00 (site timezone) or with Z / +02:00 (that instant). A bad date is 422 invalid_date.

scope.description: pipeline (posts the content pipeline produced) or all.

tools.name: syteops_calendar_next_slot
tools.description: Read-only. The next free publishing moment on the site's cadence after a time (SyteOps calendar.cadence_next_slot; SyteOps 1.6.758+). enabled is false and the slot empty when cadence is off; truncated means the calendar could not be read completely. scope is all (default) or pipeline. Returns {enabled, truncated, slot_gmt, slot_site}. Returns 409 module_unavailable when Content Pipelines is not active.

after.description: ISO 8601 date-time to search after (default now).

exclude_post_id.description: Post ID kept out of its own conflicts.

scope.description: pipeline (posts the content pipeline produced) or all.

tools.name: syteops_calendar_query
tools.description: Read-only. The publishing calendar for a window (SyteOps calendar.query; SyteOps 1.6.758+): scheduled and published posts in it (grid_events) plus the undated draft and pending rail. The window may span at most 92 days (422 range_too_large; 422 invalid_range when to is before from). scope is pipeline (default) or all. grid_truncated is true when the window held more than 500 posts: narrow it. The rail is not date-bounded: page it with rail_cursor (422 invalid_cursor) and rail_per. A site-local time the clocks skip is 422 date_in_dst_gap. Returns {from_gmt, to_gmt, scope, grid_events[], grid_truncated, rail_drafts[], rail_has_more, rail_next_cursor, rail_truncated}. Returns 409 module_unavailable when Content Pipelines is not active.

from.description: Window start: YYYY-MM-DD (start of that day) or an ISO 8601 date-time, in the site timezone unless it has Z or an offset.

to.description: Window end: YYYY-MM-DD (end of that day) or an ISO 8601 date-time. At most 92 days after from (422 range_too_large).

scope.description: pipeline (posts the content pipeline produced) or all.

post_types.description: List of calendar post type names, e.g. ["post","page"]; a keyed object or an unknown type is 422 invalid_post_type.

rail_cursor.description: rail_next_cursor from the previous page, unchanged; anything else is 422 invalid_cursor.

tools.name: syteops_calendar_reschedule
tools.description: Move a post's publication to a future moment, as dragging it on the calendar does (SyteOps calendar.reschedule; SyteOps 1.6.758+): a draft or pending post becomes scheduled and goes live by itself at that time (no review approval, readiness check or confirm), a scheduled post moves, and the schedule notice goes to the people the portal tells. date must be at least five minutes ahead (422 date_not_future); a date under five minutes ahead is refused, never published immediately; a live post cannot get a later date (409 published_immutable). A bad date is 422 invalid_date. Returns {post_id, status, scheduled, intent, date_gmt, date_site, notify}. Returns 409 module_unavailable when Content Pipelines is not active.

date.description: ISO 8601 date-time, e.g. 2026-11-03T09:00:00 (site timezone) or with Z / +02:00 (that instant). A bad date is 422 invalid_date.

tools.name: syteops_calendar_reserve_slot

Other statuses are 409 not_holdable; a post type the calendar does not handle is 422 unsupported_type. Not reserving is an answer: reserved is false with reason slots_disabled, cadence_opt_out or not_reserved. Returns {post_id, reserved, reason, slot_gmt, slot_site}. Returns 409 module_unavailable when Content Pipelines is not active.

tools.name: syteops_calendar_unpublish

Needs confirm:true. 409 not_published when it is not live; the static front page and posts page are 409 protected_page. The publication date is kept; pending post-publish recipe runs and social sends are stood down. Returns {post_id, status, previous_status}. Returns 409 module_unavailable when Content Pipelines is not active.

confirm.description: Required (true): this takes the live post down.

tools.name: syteops_calendar_unschedule

Reversible: previous_gmt is returned and syteops_calendar_reschedule puts it back. Returns {post_id, status, previous_gmt, notify}. enabled.description: true turns LLMS Amplifier on as the GEO engine, false off.

tools.name: syteops_pipeline_mode_get
tools.description: Read-only. The Content Pipelines operating mode (SyteOps pipelines.mode_get; SyteOps 1.6.758+): setup or production. Setup holds back run-history rows (activity rows are still recorded), forwarding to the workflow, social sends (held until production, not dropped) and the ingest reviewer, Now live, schedule-change and held-source alert emails, and forces new ingested posts to draft; review approvals and scheduled posts still publish in setup. Returns {mode}. Returns 409 module_unavailable when Content Pipelines are disabled in SyteOps.

Production starts workflow forwards and social sends and lets ingested posts publish. Setup holds back run history, forwards, social sends (held until production) and the ingest reviewer, Now live, schedule-change and held-source alert emails, and forces ingested posts to draft, but it does not stop syteops_review_approve or scheduled posts, which still publish. Returns 409 module_unavailable when Content Pipelines are disabled in SyteOps.

mode.description: setup (holds back run history, workflow forwarding, social sends (queued until production) and the ingest reviewer, Now live, schedule-change and held-source alert emails; new ingested posts stay drafts; review approvals and scheduled posts still publish) or production (everything live). Anything else is 422 invalid_mode.

An unknown recipe_id errors unknown_recipe. Returns {status, post_id, recipe, stages, run_id, changed}. Returns 409 module_unavailable when Content Pipelines are disabled in SyteOps.

Returns 409 module_unavailable when Content Pipelines are disabled in SyteOps.

tools.name: syteops_recipe_create

A busy write lock answers 409 save_failed: retry. A recipe is a list of stages, a trigger and a policy; copy the shape from syteops_recipe_get. On publish only the single highest-priority matching auto_publish recipe runs. Returns the saved recipe. Returns 409 module_unavailable when Content Pipelines are disabled in SyteOps.

id.description: Recipe id (a slug). Omit to derive it from name. An id that already exists is refused with 409 recipe_exists.

priority.description: Recipe priority (default 0). Only the single highest-priority matching auto_publish recipe runs on publish, so a priority above the default recipe displaces it.

options.description: Stage options; unknown keys are dropped.

trigger.description: {mode: 'auto_publish' (default) or 'manual', scope: {post_types: [..] (default ['post']), tag_slugs: [..]}}. Omitted, it defaults to auto_publish on posts. Supplied on update, it replaces the whole trigger, so send every key.

policy.description: {on_error: 'continue' (default) or 'stop', rerun: 'always' (default) or 'skip_unchanged', execution: 'async' (default) or 'sync', dry_run: bool}. Supplied on update, it replaces the whole policy, so send every key.

The deletion leaves a lasting recipe_deleted row in the Content Pipelines activity log. Returns 409 module_unavailable when Content Pipelines are disabled in SyteOps. SyteOps requires a SyteOps Admin for this delete.

tools.name: syteops_recipe_get
tools.description: Get one pipeline recipe by id (SyteOps pipelines.get_recipe). Read-only. Errors not_found for an unknown id. Returns 409 module_unavailable when Content Pipelines are disabled in SyteOps.

tools.name: syteops_recipe_list

tools.name: syteops_recipe_update
tools.description: Update a pipeline recipe (SyteOps pipelines.update_recipe). A merge-patch at the top level only: omitted keys are kept, but a supplied trigger or policy replaces that whole sub-object, so send the full sub-object to change one field (read it with syteops_recipe_get first). This is the tool that replaces a recipe by id. Errors not_found (404) for an unknown id. Returns the saved recipe. Returns 409 module_unavailable when Content Pipelines are disabled in SyteOps.

priority.description: Recipe priority (default 0). Only the single highest-priority matching auto_publish recipe runs on publish, so a priority above the default recipe displaces it.

stages.description: Ordered list of stages: {stage_id, enabled (default true), options}. An item without stage_id is silently dropped. On update the list REPLACES all stages, so send the full list (copy from syteops_recipe_get).

options.description: Stage options; unknown keys are dropped.

trigger.description: {mode: 'auto_publish' (default) or 'manual', scope: {post_types: [..] (default ['post']), tag_slugs: [..]}}. Omitted, it defaults to auto_publish on posts. Supplied on update, it replaces the whole trigger, so send every key.

policy.description: {on_error: 'continue' (default) or 'stop', rerun: 'always' (default) or 'skip_unchanged', execution: 'async' (default) or 'sync', dry_run: bool}. Supplied on update, it replaces the whole policy, so send every key.

tools.name: syteops_review_approve
tools.description: DESTRUCTIVE: approves a post for publishing (SyteOps review.approve; SyteOps 1.6.758+), as the Review Portal's Publish does with nothing edited. It publishes now, or schedules it when the post holds a reviewer's intended time or a reserved cadence slot at least a minute ahead. Needs confirm:true. Only posts sent for review (409 not_in_review). A post already live is ok with changed:false and already_live:true. It acts with SyteOps Admin authority: the post's reviewer list and who_can_publish are NOT checked for this caller. Still enforced: in review, readiness (409 not_ready with failed[] requirements), 409 published_immutable, 500 publish_failed. Open notes do not block it; open_notes reports them. It takes no as_user_id: the approver is the API key (user 0) or the signed-in SyteOps Admin. Returns {post_id, status, scheduled, permalink, emailed, notify, images, open_notes, approved_by, already_live}. Returns 409 module_unavailable when the Review Portal is not loaded.

confirm.description: Required (true): this puts the post live (or schedules it).

tools.name: syteops_review_comment_add
tools.description: Add a review note as one person through the Review Portal's own writer (SyteOps review.comments_add; SyteOps 1.6.758+). Send exactly one target: parent_id (a reply to a top-level note; notify and resolve apply), attachment_id or image_url (a note on a picture), or element (a note pinned to a page element). None is 422 target_required, more than one is 422 ambiguous_target; for an article-level note use syteops_review_request_changes. The note is marked as added via API. Through MCP omit as_user_id to act as yourself (the SyteOps Admin); pass it only to act on behalf of that user (SyteOps's own REST API key must send it; MCP need not). That person must be able to comment (403 forbidden); resolve needs edit rights. Returns {post_id, as_user_id, kind, entry}; a reply adds {resolve, notified, notify}. Returns 409 module_unavailable when the Review Portal is not loaded.

as_user_id.description: User ID to act as. Through MCP omit as_user_id to act as yourself (the SyteOps Admin); pass it only to act on behalf of that user. (The 422 as_user_id_required rule applies to the SyteOps REST API key, not to MCP.)

parent_id.description: Reply to this top-level note id (a reply target).

notify.description: Reply only: email the thread (default true).

resolve.description: Reply only: also resolve the parent note (needs edit rights).

attachment_id.description: Attachment ID of the picture (a picture target).

image_url.description: The picture's URL, when it has no attachment ID (a picture target).

element.description: Element target (an element note). Keys: selector, sig, text, ox, oy, vw, media, src, name, breakpoint, tag, el_id, classes, heading, html, builder_path, rect, url, bld; any other key is 422 invalid_params.

tools.name: syteops_review_comments
tools.description: Read-only. One post's review notes and replies, oldest first, as the portal shows them (SyteOps review.comments_list; SyteOps 1.6.750+). Returns {post_id, total, page, per_page, has_more, comments[]}; a comment is {id, parent, user_id, user_name, note, created_at, kind, target_kind, att_id, resolved}. Returns 409 module_unavailable when the Review Portal is not loaded.

tools.name: syteops_review_get
tools.description: Read-only. One post's review status (SyteOps review.get; SyteOps 1.6.750+): post status, whether changes are requested, open and total note counts, the reviewers and watchers, and the latest recorded activity. A missing, trashed or non-viewable post is 404 post_not_found. Returns {post_id, title, post_status, changes_requested, open_notes, total_notes, reviewers[], watchers[], last_activity: {event, at} or null}; a person is {user_id, display_name, roles[]}. Returns 409 module_unavailable when the Review Portal is not loaded.

tools.name: syteops_review_permissions_get
tools.description: Read-only. The Review Portal's Portal Permissions as the settings screen reads them (SyteOps review.permissions_get; SyteOps 1.6.758+): who_can_publish (any or author_approver), the per-area matrix (default row, role rows by SyteOps role slug, person rows by user number; an absent cell inherits), every area with its allowed values and whether this site shows it, and the role and person rows that may be set. Works before the portal is in use. Read it before syteops_review_permissions_set.

tools.name: syteops_review_permissions_set
tools.description: DESTRUCTIVE: changes who can review and publish in the Review Portal (SyteOps review.permissions_set; SyteOps 1.6.758+). Needs confirm:true. Read syteops_review_permissions_get first. Partial, cell-level merge: only the cells sent change. In roles and users a cell of "inherit" or null clears it and a row of null clears the row; default takes real values only; only people linked to a WordPress account can be set. Send permissions, who_can_publish or both (422 nothing_to_change). 422 invalid_permissions (nothing is written) and invalid_who_can_publish; 409 no_publisher_left (author_approver with no administrator publish override); 409 busy (a concurrent set; retry). Returns {who_can_publish, permissions, changes[]}.

permissions.description: Partial matrix: {default?: {area: value}, roles?: {slug: {area: value|"inherit"|null}|null}, users?: {user_num: {area: value|"inherit"|null}|null}}. Only the cells sent change; "inherit" or null clears a role or person cell, a null row clears the row; default takes real values only.

who_can_publish.description: any (any selected reviewer) or author_approver (the post author or an administrator).

confirm.description: Required (true): this changes who can publish.

tools.name: syteops_review_queue
tools.description: Read-only. One page of a person's Review Portal queue, as that person sees it (SyteOps review.queue_list; SyteOps 1.6.750+). list is pending (default), watching, live, live_posts, live_pages, coming_up or notes; per_page is 5, 10, 25 or 100; page on with the returned next_cursor. as_user_id is the person whose queue to read: SyteOps requires it on an API-key call (422 as_user_id_required), but this tool runs in-process as a SyteOps Admin, so it may be omitted and then reads that admin's own queue; an unknown user is 404 user_not_found, and an over-long cursor is 422 invalid_cursor. Rows carry no review links or tokens. Returns {as_user_id, list, rows[], has_more, next_cursor, truncated, page_count}. A post row is {post_id, title, source, received, scheduled_ts, modified_ts, feedback_count, changes_requested, qa}; a notes row is {post_id, title, author, excerpt, created, note_id}. Returns 409 module_unavailable when the Review Portal is not loaded.

as_user_id.description: User ID whose queue to read. Through MCP omit as_user_id to read your own queue (the SyteOps Admin); pass it to read that user's. (SyteOps's own REST API key must send it; MCP need not.)

list.description: Which list: pending (default), watching, live, live_posts, live_pages, coming_up or notes.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page, at most 512 characters.

tools.name: syteops_review_request_changes
tools.description: Send a post back for changes as one person (SyteOps review.request_changes; SyteOps 1.6.758+): records message as their note, cancels a pending schedule when they may publish, and emails the author and co-reviewers. The note is marked as added via API. Through MCP omit as_user_id to act as yourself (the SyteOps Admin); pass it only to act on behalf of that user (422 as_user_id_required applies to SyteOps's own REST API key, not to MCP). That person must be able to edit the post (403 forbidden); 409 schedule_due when it is about to publish and they cannot cancel it. Returns {post_id, as_user_id, entry, emailed, notify, unscheduled, status}. Returns 409 module_unavailable when the Review Portal is not loaded.

as_user_id.description: User ID to act as. Through MCP omit as_user_id to act as yourself (the SyteOps Admin); pass it only to act on behalf of that user. (The 422 as_user_id_required rule applies to the SyteOps REST API key, not to MCP.)

tools.name: syteops_review_reviewer_add
tools.description: Add a reviewer to one post (SyteOps review.reviewers_add; SyteOps 1.6.758+). This grants that person edit rights on the post through the Review Portal, and publish rights too unless who_can_publish is author_approver (then only the author or an administrator can publish), and emails them; the review link gets a fresh expiry. user_id must be a SyteOps user linked to a WordPress account (422 user_not_selectable; 404 user_not_found). A post never sent for review is 409 not_review_managed. A watcher added as a reviewer stops being a watcher. Someone already listed is ok with changed:false and is not emailed again. Returns {post_id, user_id, emailed, notify, reviewers[], watchers[]}. Returns 409 module_unavailable when the Review Portal is not loaded.

user_id.description: User ID of a SyteOps user linked to a WordPress account.

tools.name: syteops_review_reviewer_remove
tools.description: Remove a reviewer from one post (SyteOps review.reviewers_remove; SyteOps 1.6.758+). They lose portal access to it unless something else grants it (site administrator, watcher, bundle reviewer). The post's author cannot be removed (409 author_protected). The removal sticks: source default reviewers and CCs do not put them back. Someone not listed is ok with changed:false. No email is sent. Returns {post_id, user_id, reviewers[], watchers[]}. Returns 409 module_unavailable when the Review Portal is not loaded.

user_id.description: User ID of a SyteOps user linked to a WordPress account.

tools.name: syteops_review_reviewers
tools.description: Read-only. The people who may review one post and the people watching it (SyteOps review.reviewers_get; SyteOps 1.6.750+). Ids, display names and roles only; no email addresses. Returns {post_id, reviewers[], watchers[]}; a person is {user_id, display_name, roles[]}. Returns 409 module_unavailable when the Review Portal is not loaded.

tools.name: syteops_review_watcher_add
tools.description: Add a watcher to one post (SyteOps review.watchers_add; SyteOps 1.6.758+): they may open it, comment and get its routine review emails, but cannot edit or publish. user_id must be a SyteOps user linked to a WordPress account (422 user_not_selectable). A post never sent for review is 409 not_review_managed; a reviewer of the post is 409 already_reviewer. Someone already watching is ok with changed:false. No email is sent. Returns {post_id, user_id, reviewers[], watchers[]}. Returns 409 module_unavailable when the Review Portal is not loaded.

user_id.description: User ID of a SyteOps user linked to a WordPress account.

tools.name: syteops_review_watcher_remove
tools.description: Remove a watcher from one post (SyteOps review.watchers_remove; SyteOps 1.6.758+). They can no longer open or comment on it unless something else grants that. The removal sticks: source default CCs do not put them back. Someone not watching is ok with changed:false. No email is sent. Returns {post_id, user_id, reviewers[], watchers[]}. Returns 409 module_unavailable when the Review Portal is not loaded.

user_id.description: User ID of a SyteOps user linked to a WordPress account.

tools.name: syteops_seo_get
tools.description: Read one post's SEO title, description and focus keywords from whichever SEO plugin is active (SyteOps seo.get). Returns {post_id, tool, tool_label, fields}. With no active SEO plugin it errors no_active_seo_tool. For Squirrly-only fields (canonical, Open Graph, robots) use sqseo_get_snippet.

tools.name: syteops_seo_set
tools.description: Write one post's SEO title, description or focus keywords through the active SEO plugin's own writer (SyteOps seo.set). SEO writes for any SEO plugin go here, not update_content.meta. Send dry_run:true first: it writes nothing and returns each field's current and proposed value. A real write needs confirm:true. Only the fields you send change. Caps: title 300, description 1000, keywords 500 characters. A placeholder the SEO plugin fills from site data is refused unless allow_placeholders:true. On Squirrly the result carries a note: reload any block-editor tab that was open before the write, or its SEO Snippet box saves the old title back. For Squirrly-only fields use sqseo_set_snippet.

title.description: SEO title. Send an empty string to clear it.

description.description: Meta description. Send an empty string to clear it.

keywords.description: Focus keywords, comma-separated. Send an empty string to clear it.

dry_run.description: Preview only; nothing is written.

confirm.description: Required (true) for a real write.

allow_placeholders.description: JSON true only. Allow placeholders the SEO plugin fills from site data (custom fields, options). Safe ones such as the post title need no opt-in.

tools.name: syteops_social_cancel
tools.description: Cancel one scheduled social send on an article by the job_id syteops_social_schedule returned (SyteOps social.cancel; SyteOps 1.6.758+). Works while Social Publishing is off. 404 post_not_found; 404 job_not_found when no such job is pending. Returns {post_id, job_id, cancelled}. Returns 409 module_unavailable when Social Publishing is not loaded.

tools.name: syteops_social_schedule
tools.description: Queue one social send for one article to a configured destination (SyteOps social.schedule; SyteOps 1.6.758+). when is time (default; sends at fire_at) or on_publish (sends when the article first goes live; fire_at is then 422 invalid_params). 409 social_disabled while Social Publishing is off; 422 bad_destination; 422 already_published (on_publish for an article already live); a send due while the pipeline is in setup mode is held and retried hourly until production; 404 post_not_found; a signed-in caller also needs publish rights on the post type (403 forbidden). Returns {post_id, job_id, when, fire_at, destination}; keep job_id to cancel. Returns 409 module_unavailable when Social Publishing is not loaded.

destination_id.description: A configured social destination ID (unknown is 422 bad_destination).

text.description: The final post text, at most 3000 characters (422 text_too_long; empty is 422 empty_text).

when.description: time (default; send at fire_at) or on_publish (send when the article first goes live; fire_at not allowed).

fire_at.description: Unix time in seconds, between one minute and five years ahead (422 bad_time / too_far). Needed when when is time.

tools.name: syteops_source_approve_mapping
tools.description: Approve a field mapping for a content source, activating it for live ingest (SyteOps content_sources.approve_mapping). Returns {id, status, mapping_status, mapping}.

mapping.description: The field mapping to approve and activate for live ingest.

tools.name: syteops_source_create
tools.description: Create a content source (SyteOps content_sources.create); SyteOps generates its id and slug. Unless you pass a secret or auth_mode:'none', it generates a webhook secret and returns it as data.secret (only when secret_source is 'generated'), once. The plaintext secret is not redacted and is returned only once: do not log or store it. The slug comes from name and cannot be changed later. A supplied secret or forward_secret is write-only.

name.description: Source name; the slug is derived from it.

auth_mode.description: Inbound verification: 'hmac' (default), 'bearer', 'both' or 'none' (no verification; the slug URL is the only gate). Switching from 'none' to a verifying mode with no stored secret errors secret_required.

secret.description: Write-only verification secret, e.g. a provider-owned key. Never echoed back.

pin_author.description: Pin the default author on ingested posts.

new_cpt.description: Source-owned custom post type definition. Create-time only; not editable afterwards.

meta_fields.description: Native custom fields this source declares: a list of {field_key, label, type}.

fm_variables.description: Per-source FlowMattic config vars: a list of {key, value, source: 'payload' or 'static'}.

forward_enabled.description: Forward each ingest to a workflow URL.

forward_url.description: Workflow URL to forward to. Must pass wp_http_validate_url: private hosts and unusual ports are rejected.

forward_auth_mode.description: Auth mode for the forward call.

forward_secret.description: Write-only forward secret; never returned on any read.

author_match_mode.description: How the incoming author is matched.

target_tag_slug.description: Tag slug applied to ingested posts. Changing it on update retags this source's existing posts.

category_exclude.description: Category slugs the AI classifier may never choose: a list of strings.

strip_inbody_toc.description: Strip an in-body table of contents.

tools.name: syteops_source_delete
tools.description: Permanently delete a content source (SyteOps content_sources.delete). Needs confirm:true. Returns {id, deleted}. SyteOps requires a SyteOps Admin for this delete.

confirm.description: Required (true): SyteOps refuses the delete without it.

tools.name: syteops_source_export
tools.description: Export one content source as a portable setup package (SyteOps content_sources.export). Read-only. The envelope {format, schema_version, payload} never includes secret or forward_secret; feed it to syteops_source_import.

tools.name: syteops_source_get
tools.description: Get one content source by id (SyteOps content_sources.get). Read-only. Secrets are never included.

tools.name: syteops_source_import
tools.description: Import a content source setup package (SyteOps content_sources.import). When the slug is free it creates the source; when it exists it errors already_exists. To replace an existing source send overwrite:true AND confirm:true (overwrite alone errors confirmation_required); an overwrite clears the stored forward_secret and, for a verifying auth_mode, also invalidates the source's current webhook secret and returns the new one once, so live senders break until updated. This op is not marked destructive, so confirm only gates that overwrite. If a verifying secret is minted it is returned as data.secret (only when secret_source is 'generated'). The plaintext secret is not redacted and is returned only once: do not log or store it.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing source with the same slug. Also needs confirm:true.

confirm.description: Required (true) together with overwrite to replace an existing source.

tools.name: syteops_source_learn
tools.description: Ask the Ingest AI area to propose a field mapping from the source's captured sample (SyteOps content_sources.learn_from_sample; SyteOps 1.6.758+). The proposal REPLACES the stored mapping and is never approved: on a source whose mapping was approved, new deliveries are held until it is approved again, so that call needs confirm:true (409 confirmation_required). Spends an AI call and shares the source's daily AI allowance (default 10 a day, UTC) with syteops_source_reprocess (429 learn_cap_reached). 404 not_found; 409 no_provider or no_sample; 422 invalid_sample; 502 ai_empty_response or invalid_json; 503 ai_unavailable. Returns {mapping}.

confirm.description: Required (true) when the source's mapping is approved.

tools.name: syteops_source_list
tools.description: List all content sources, the inbound feeds that create posts for the pipelines (SyteOps content_sources.list). Read-only. Each has id, name, slug, enabled, status, auth_mode, target_post_type, mapping, mapping_status, defaults and forward settings. Secrets are never included.

tools.name: syteops_source_reprocess
tools.description: DESTRUCTIVE: replays a source's last captured payload through the ingest core (SyteOps content_sources.reprocess; SyteOps 1.6.758+). Needs confirm:true. It creates or updates the article with the source's own settings: a source set to publish publishes it, a source in overwrite mode overwrites reviewer edits on an article already live, and the draft core spends an AI call. Shares the source's daily AI allowance (default 10 a day, UTC) with syteops_source_learn (429 learn_cap_reached). 404 not_found (unknown or disabled source); 409 no_payload; 422 invalid_json. Returns {outcome, message, post_id, created, edit_link}; changed is false for a held or protected article.

confirm.description: Required (true): this can publish or overwrite an article.

tools.name: syteops_source_resend_review_email
tools.description: Re-send the review email for a post to its own reviewers, never to a caller-supplied address (SyteOps content_sources.resend_review_email; SyteOps 1.6.758+). One resend per post every 120 seconds (429 resend_cooldown). 404 post_not_found; 400 no_recipients; 500 send_failed. Returns {message, notify} with display names only. Returns 409 module_unavailable when the Review Portal is not loaded.

tools.name: syteops_source_rotate_secret
tools.description: Generate a new webhook secret for a content source and invalidate the old one at once (SyteOps content_sources.rotate_secret). Returns {id, secret} with the new secret, once; it enters this conversation's transcript. The plaintext secret is not redacted and is returned only once: do not log or store it. Senders using the old secret fail until updated.

tools.name: syteops_source_test
tools.description: Read-only preview of a mapping against a sample payload; nothing is written (SyteOps content_sources.test; SyteOps 1.6.758+). Omit mapping to test the source's stored mapping. An empty sample is 422 no_sample; 404 not_found. Returns {normalized, empty_fields}.

sample.description: The sample payload, as a non-empty JSON object (an empty one is 422 no_sample).

mapping.description: Optional field => {path, transform} rows to try; omit to test the source's stored mapping.

tools.name: syteops_source_update
tools.description: Update editable fields on a content source (SyteOps content_sources.update); only the fields you send change. The slug, new_cpt and the internal idempotency key are not editable. A non-empty secret or forward_secret overwrites the stored one (write-only, never returned); an empty value leaves it unchanged. Returns the source without secrets.

pin_author.description: Pin the default author on ingested posts.

default_reviewers.description: Default reviewers for ingested posts: a list of WordPress user IDs (integers).

default_ccs.description: Default CC recipients for ingested posts: a list of WordPress user IDs (integers).

default_post_status.description: 'draft' (default) or 'publish'; anything else is stored as draft.

auth_mode.description: Inbound verification: 'hmac' (default), 'bearer', 'both' or 'none' (no verification; the slug URL is the only gate). Switching from 'none' to a verifying mode with no stored secret errors secret_required.

secret.description: Write-only verification secret, e.g. a provider-owned key. Never echoed back.

meta_fields.description: Native custom fields this source declares: a list of {field_key, label, type}.

fm_variables.description: Per-source FlowMattic config vars: a list of {key, value, source: 'payload' or 'static'}.

forward_enabled.description: Forward each ingest to a workflow URL.

forward_url.description: Workflow URL to forward to. Must pass wp_http_validate_url: private hosts and unusual ports are rejected.

forward_auth_mode.description: Auth mode for the forward call.

forward_secret.description: Write-only forward secret; never returned on any read.

author_match_mode.description: How the incoming author is matched.

target_tag_slug.description: Tag slug applied to ingested posts. Changing it on update retags this source's existing posts.

category_exclude.description: Category slugs the AI classifier may never choose: a list of strings.

strip_inbody_toc.description: Strip an in-body table of contents.

tools.name: sytewide_bulk
tools.description: Run one tool repeatedly over a list of argument sets and return the per-call results. Capped at 50 calls per request. For destructive target tools, include "dry_run": true in each call to preview.

tool.description: Name of the tool to invoke for each item.

calls.description: Array of argument objects, one per invocation (max 50).

dry_run.description: If true, preview the whole batch: dry_run is propagated into every call so destructive target tools are previewed, not executed.

tools.name: sytewide_get_status
tools.description: Report SyteWide MCP server status: version, current WordPress user, active tool providers, and total registered tool count.

tools.name: sytewide_ping
tools.description: Health check. Returns "pong" and the server time to confirm the SyteWide MCP connection is live.

tools.name: update_comment
tools.description: Update a comment (content or status). Only provided fields change.

tools.name: update_content
tools.description: Update existing content of any type. Only provided fields change.

meta.description: Meta registered for the REST API. Other keys are not saved and come back in warnings. For SEO fields use syteops_seo_set.

dry_run.description: If true, preview this destructive action without executing it.

tools.name: update_option_value
tools.description: Change ONE existing scalar value inside a WordPress option: reads the option, sets that leaf, saves with update_option (autoload unchanged), then reads back. If the leaf took, it returns verified:true, plus concurrent_change_detected:true and changed_count (a number; no key names) when another key also changed; nothing is reverted. If the leaf did not take, only that leaf is set back and the call fails. Not atomic: a write by someone else between the read and the save is lost. Send value (the leaf keeps its type: an int takes an integral number or numeric string, a float any number, a bool only true/false, a string a string or integer) or increment (an integer, int leaves only). Never creates an option or key and never writes an array or object. Refused: leaves that get_option_value would hide (strings and numbers under credential-shaped names or records; bools are writable), credential-shaped values (set secrets with wp-cli in a terminal so they stay out of the transcript), options whose reads are filtered (pre_option_/option_ hooks) or differ from the stored row or its name casing, hard-denied options, WordPress core options, SyteOps options (use the syteops_* tools), SyteWide options, role/capability/permission/level data, and credential-row paths outside the allowlist. Defaults to a dry run returning {option, path, old, new, type}; a real write needs dry_run:false AND confirm:true.

path.description: Key path inside the option. An array of keys is preferred, e.g. ["rates", 0, "label"], and is required when a key contains a dot; a dot-path string "rates.0.label" also works. Omit for the whole option.

value.description: New scalar value. Not with increment.

increment.description: Add this to an int leaf (negative to subtract). Not with value.

dry_run.description: Default true: preview only. Pass false (with confirm:true) to write.

confirm.description: Required (true), together with dry_run:false, for a real write.

tools.name: update_plugin
tools.description: Update an installed plugin to its latest version via the WordPress upgrader (there is no core REST route for plugin updates). Pass the plugin file path including .php, e.g. akismet/akismet.php.

plugin.description: Plugin file basename including .php, e.g. akismet/akismet.php.

dry_run.description: If true, preview this destructive action without executing it.

tools.name: update_term
tools.description: Update an existing taxonomy term.

tools.name: update_user
tools.description: Update an existing WordPress user. Only provided fields change.

tools.name: wc_analytics_list_routes
tools.description: List the WooCommerce Analytics REST routes registered under /wc-analytics and their HTTP methods. Optional "search" substring filter and "limit" (1-500, default 200). Use this to find a path for wc_analytics_request.

search.description: Only return routes whose path contains this substring.

tools.name: wc_analytics_request
tools.description: Call any WooCommerce Analytics REST route (scoped to /wc-analytics). GET runs immediately; POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE require "confirm": true, or pass "dry_run": true to preview the request. Use wc_analytics_list_routes to discover available paths.

method.description: HTTP method: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE.

path.description: Route path within /wc-analytics, e.g. /wc-analytics/<resource> for a collection or /wc-analytics/<resource>/42 for one item. Call wc_analytics_list_routes for the real resource names — do not guess them.

confirm.description: Required to execute a write (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE).

dry_run.description: Preview a write without executing it.

tools.name: wc_get_settings_group
tools.description: Read the options in ONE WooCommerce settings group, with each option's id, current value, default and type. Returns only that group's own options — NOT its children's: settings groups are hierarchical, so stock options are in "inventory" rather than "products", and per-email options are in the email_* groups. If an option you expect is missing, check the group's sub_groups via wc_list_settings_groups. Store address and currency live in "general"; tax posture lives in "tax".

group.description: Settings group id, e.g. general, products, tax, shipping.

tools.name: wc_get_shipping_zone
tools.description: Get one WooCommerce shipping zone with its locations and shipping methods resolved. Use this to read the current location set before calling wc_set_shipping_zone_locations.

zone_id.description: Shipping zone ID (0 is "Locations not covered by your other zones").

tools.name: wc_list_routes
tools.description: List the WooCommerce REST routes registered under /wc/v3 and their HTTP methods. Optional "search" substring filter and "limit" (1-500, default 200). Use this to find a path for wc_request.

search.description: Only return routes whose path contains this substring.

tools.name: wc_list_settings_groups
tools.description: List the WooCommerce settings groups (general, products, tax, shipping, checkout, account, email, advanced, integration, plus any an extension has added). Groups are HIERARCHICAL: the response is one flat list in which child groups carry a "parent_id" and parents carry "sub_groups". Options live on whichever group actually owns them — stock settings are in "inventory" (a child of products), not in "products" — so read sub_groups before concluding an option does not exist.

tools.name: wc_list_shipping_zones
tools.description: List WooCommerce shipping zones with each zone's locations and shipping methods resolved in one call. Includes zone 0 ("Locations not covered by your other zones"), which has methods but no locations. Resolving costs one request per zone per sub-resource, so set include_locations or include_methods to false, or lower "limit", on stores with many zones.

include_methods.description: Resolve each zone's shipping methods (default true).

limit.description: Max zones to resolve (1-200, default 50). The response reports total and truncated.

tools.name: wc_request
tools.description: Call any WooCommerce REST route (scoped to /wc/v3). GET runs immediately; POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE require "confirm": true, or pass "dry_run": true to preview the request. Use wc_list_routes to discover available paths.

method.description: HTTP method: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE.

path.description: Route path within /wc/v3, e.g. /wc/v3/<resource> for a collection or /wc/v3/<resource>/42 for one item. Call wc_list_routes for the real resource names — do not guess them.

confirm.description: Required to execute a write (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE).

dry_run.description: Preview a write without executing it.

tools.name: wc_set_shipping_zone_locations
tools.description: Replace a shipping zone's ENTIRE location set. WooCommerce's underlying PUT replaces every location on the zone — it does NOT merge — so "locations" must be the complete intended set, not just the additions. Read the current set with wc_get_shipping_zone first. WooCommerce silently discards entries with a missing code or an unrecognized type, so the response reports added/removed/rejected computed against what WooCommerce actually stored. Pass an empty array to clear every location. Zone 0 cannot be edited.

zone_id.description: Shipping zone ID. Zone 0 ("Locations not covered by your other zones") cannot be edited.

locations.description: The COMPLETE intended location set. Each entry MUST be an object with a non-empty "code" and a "type" of exactly postcode, state, country or continent (lowercase — WooCommerce compares strictly). Example: { "code": "US:HI", "type": "state" }.

code.description: Location code, e.g. US:HI for a state, US for a country, 96813 for a postcode.

type.description: One of postcode, state, country, continent.

dry_run.description: If true, preview this destructive action without executing it.

tools.name: wc_system_status
tools.description: Read the WooCommerce system status report — environment, database state, active plugins, theme and template overrides, settings and page setup. The full report is very large, so pass "sections" to keep only the parts you need; omit it to get everything.

sections.description: Top-level sections to keep, e.g. ["environment","theme"]. Must be an array, not a bare string. Sections: environment, database, active_plugins, inactive_plugins, dropins_mu_plugins, theme, settings, security, pages, post_type_counts, logging. Omit for the whole report. The response carries a "_filter" key describing what was kept, dropped and available.

tools.name: wc_update_setting
tools.description: Set one WooCommerce setting. Options are addressed by group AND option id (e.g. group "general", option_id "woocommerce_currency") — read the group first with wc_get_settings_group to get the exact id and the value shape it expects. Changes take effect on the live storefront immediately.

option_id.description: Option id within the group, e.g. woocommerce_currency.

value.description: New value. Type must match what the option expects (string, boolean, or array) — check wc_get_settings_group.

dry_run.description: If true, preview this destructive action without executing it.

tools.name: wc_update_shipping_method
tools.description: Update a shipping method instance on a zone. Method-specific configuration (cost, tax status, min-amount) goes inside the nested "settings" object, keyed by setting id with a PLAIN SCALAR value — e.g. { "cost": "9.95" }. Note the read/write asymmetry: wc_get_shipping_zone returns each setting as an object ({ id, label, type, value }); send back only the value, not that object. Only the fields you pass are sent.

instance_id.description: Method instance ID on that zone (from wc_get_shipping_zone).

enabled.description: Enable or disable this method instance.

settings.description: Method settings keyed by setting id, each a plain scalar value, e.g. { "cost": "9.95", "tax_status": "taxable" }.

dry_run.description: If true, preview this destructive action without executing it.

tools.name: wp_list_routes
tools.description: List the WordPress REST REST routes registered under /wp/v2 and their HTTP methods. Optional "search" substring filter and "limit" (1-500, default 200). Use this to find a path for wp_request.

search.description: Only return routes whose path contains this substring.
